title: Decode Whisper with your own loops
brief: Build Whisper's forced prompt, greedy and beam-search decoding over any decoder's logits, the timestamp rules, a Whisper-style text normalizer, and corpus WER, then transcribe LibriSpeech with whisper-tiny.
hints: build_prompt is three or four dictionary lookups; the language id comes from LANGUAGES and the task id from SPECIAL[f'<|{task}|>'].
In greedy_decode, apply logit_filter before the log-softmax, so the summed log-probability is measured on the filtered distribution, the way Whisper measures it.
For beam_search_decode, key a dictionary by tuple(tokens) so identical extensions from two beams collapse into one entry, then walk sorted(candidates, key=candidates.get, reverse=True).
A finished hypothesis's length for ranking is the number of tokens before eot. Divide its summed log-probability by max(length, 1).
apply_timestamp_rules works on a copy: np.array(logits, dtype=float). Apply the rules in the docstring's order, because rule 5 measures the mass left after rules 1 to 4.
np.logaddexp.reduce over the timestamp log-probabilities gives the log of their total probability.
In normalize_text, the regular expression [^\w\s]|_ matches every character that is neither a letter, a digit, nor whitespace.
